scope: Design/runbook and scratch fixture only; no product source changes. Private homes and loopback transport fixtures only; no Fleet/HubRuntime/service or external directory/provider start.

commands.command: npx --no-install vitest run tests/hub-host-move-m3792.test.ts tests/hub-member-relocation-3429.test.ts tests/hub-relocation-network-3429.test.ts tests/hub-member-address-writer-3429.test.ts tests/hub-install-handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
commands.note: Three scratch controls plus sixty existing neighbor cases; Vitest4.1.12.
Final scratch version adds an actual pinned-member transport connection to the cold destination. Overlaps the preceding run; counts are not additive.

proofs: Same Hub UUID, issuer and member SPKI survive a stopped copy to a different private home.
Signed initialization seal remains valid with copied matching config; arbitrary new hostname is rejected.
Database transport state/floor and authenticated encrypted content survive the copy; incomplete content-key state is rejected.
A real signed address decision preserves the acknowledged Fleet credential/generation and pairing bytes; an offline Fleet is revoked.
Confirmed B-only dialing and new B-to-A pending dialing preserve exact pairing; old identical statement retry does not undo the newer pending move.
New-host certificate preserves SPKI but fails hostname verification at A, requiring the runbook port/isolation gate.
A real pinned member pairs once, source listener and DB close, then an unchanged-origin destination using the cold copy accepts it with unchanged member pairing bytes and Fleet binding.
fixtureBoundaries: Signed-change decision ports use fixture ack-currentness/probe/remount; the separate unchanged-origin cold-copy case uses actual pinned TLS/WebSocket reconnect. Neither starts a Fleet or tests an OS service.
Existing network neighbor suite uses loopback TLS/WebSocket fixtures, not a Fleet start.
No actual OS migration, VM capacity, DNS/proxy, AD reachability, service-manager launch, account credential transfer or shared-agent answer was tested.
No cross-host exclusive lock exists; positive source stop/fencing remains an operational prerequisite.
initialProbeFindings: Copy permissions needed normalization before production private-path open accepted the destination.
An old confirmed statement is safely re-ACKed without changing a newer pending relocation; it is not necessarily refused.

A new-host SAN under the unchanged SPKI is not valid at the old hostname; same-backend-port remount can cause terminal key-changed rather than retry. The runbook requires old-ingress/new-backend isolation.
typecheck: Final typecheck passed with reused existing complete dependencies and8GiB heap; no packages installed. Initial root fallback dependency set was incomplete and default4GiB check exceeded heap.
